newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Evacuation looms as PNG volcano comes to life.
newsitem.headline: Evacuation looms as PNG volcano comes to life.

text.p: Papua New Guinea has put thousands of people on standby for evacuation after a volcano in in the South Pacific nation's northeast began spewing ash and lava, an emergency services official said on Sunday.

The Tavurvur volcano, which forced the abandonment of the nearby town of Rabaul with an eruption in 1994, began erupting again on Saturday, National Disaster and Emergency Services Director Leith Anderson told Reuters by telephone from Port Moresby.
"We've got people on standby -- they may be asked to get out if it does play up," he said.
Anderson said about 3,500 people were on alert for possible evacuation.
The volcano shot ash and lava eight kilometres (5 miles) into the air on Saturday and lava flowed down its eastern slope, Anderson said.
Although activity eased on Sunday, the alert remained.
"It's quite a spectacular display," Anderson said.

Rabaul, a port town on New Britain island 800 kilometres (500 miles) northeast of Port Moresby, was devastated in September 1994 when two volcanoes erupted, forcing the evacuation of 30,000 people and the virtual desertion of the town, which still lies buried under a deep layer of ash.
Papua New Guinea, just north of Australia, lies on the belt of volcanic activity that rings the Pacific Ocean and is known as the "Ring of Fire".
